newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain fears ETA has kidnapped politician.
newsitem.headline: Spain fears ETA has kidnapped politician.

text.p: Spain's Interior Ministry said on Thursday it feared a town councillor in the Basque region had been kidnapped by ETA Basque separatists who have threatened to kill him in 48 hours.

A caller saying he was from ETA told a director at Basque radio Egin, ETA's usual mouthpiece, that Popular Party politician Miguel Angel Blanco would be killed unless the government moved Basque prisoners nearer to their homeland.
A ministry spokesman confirmed that the call had been received and that Blanco, 29, had disappeared earlier in the day, but he could not confirm the kidnap.

"All the indications point to it, there was a call by the terrorist band ETA to Egin communicating the kidnap of Blanco and saying if the government doesn't move all the ETA prisoners closer to the Basque region before Saturday at 4 p.m. they will assassinate him," Cayetano Gonzalez said on state radio.
A spokesman for the ruling Popular Party said the government would stand firm on its policy toward the separatist guerrillas and not bend to their demands.

"Once more the Popular Party reiterates that a difference should not be made between the victims," the party said in a statement. "As a result of this conviction, we express our hope for the quick liberation of our companion, Miguel Angel Blanco."
Blanco, the town councillor for Ermua, was last seen catching a train to work at 2 p.m (1200 GMT) on Thursday, authorities said.

ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has been pushing the Popular Party government to move imprisoned members to jails in the Basque region. Under a long-standing policy, they are scattered around the country.
Last week the separatists released a kidnapped businessman and hours later Spanish police rescued a prison worker who had been held hostage by ETA for 532 days.
ETA, which has killed some 800 people in its nearly 30-year drive for Basque independence, had also abducted the prison worker to pressure the government on its ETA prison policy.
"We have not yet recovered from the cruel images of Jose Antonio Ortega Lara when again the worst inhumanity tries to return to dominate us all," Atutxa said.
Egin alerted police on Thursday afternoon immediately after the call and the ministry said an investigation had started to confirm Blanco's disappearance and kidnapping.
An hour after the first call, the same person speaking in the name of ETA telephoned again, reiterating the details of the kidnapping, authorities said.
Blanco's mother, father and girlfriend sat at home anxiously awaiting news of the politician while hundreds of people marched through Ermua in protest at the presumed kidnapping.
"This town councillor did not have an important role in the PP and ETA probably took advantage of his lack of protection," said Carlos Totorika, mayor of Ermua.
Blanco is a trained economist who works as a consultant.
